head.title: Cantique de Jean Racine
head.description: Gabriel Fauré's Cantique on Jean Racine's French paraphrase of a Latin hymn, as Fauré wrote the four voices (printed in Paris about 1876), for 4 singers, in French: slow, soft and smooth. The basses begin and the other parts come in one by one. The organ's introduction and interlude are left out (the interlude becomes a rest of a few beats).

credits.words: Jean Racine, after the Latin hymn "Consors paterni luminis"
credits.arrangement: Fauré's own four voice parts (Paris: F. Schoen, about 1876)

licence.arrangement: Fauré's own four voice parts as F. Schoen printed them in Paris about 1876 (public domain), the organ left out, with breaths written in for beginners: a line's last note gives up half a beat or a beat, and where that was not enough the next line's first syllable starts half a beat later in every part that sings it ("Di-vin" in bar 27, "que tout" in bar 44, "Dis-si-pe" in bar 47), and the bass's "nous" (bar 21) starts a beat later, with the other parts. Two of Fauré's elisions in the bass are sung apart to make room for a breath: "ble à ce" (bar 61) in the tenor's rhythm, "ble, à ce", and "gloi-re im-mor-tel-le" (bar 70) with a breath before "im-", where the tenor breathes. Left out: the organ's introduction (bars 1 to 12; the song starts on the bass's entry) and its bars 32 to 38 (the choir's rest of seven and a half bars becomes five beats); the last chord is held three beats in place of two tied bars under a fermata. Bar numbers are the print's. Accepted exceptions (singable.py and the app's check), all Fauré's own notes: the soprano's range, up to G-flat5 on "ta voix, Dis-" (bar 47), to F5 ten times more ("vin" and the held note of "Sau-" in bar 28, "son" (bar 46), "de" (bar 47), "si-" (bar 48), "la" in bars 53 and 57, "lois!" in bar 59, "de" and the held note of "tes" in bar 72) and down to D-flat4 on the last two "comblé!"; the tenor's G-flat4 on "Dis-" (bar 48) and "bli" (bar 54); four to six seconds near the top or bottom of a range in every part; the slurred notes (melismas) in the alto, tenor and bass; the leaps, among them the bass's octaves F2 to F3 (bar 23) and A-flat3 to A-flat2 (bar 78) and its tritone C3 to G-flat3 (bar 77), the tenor's sixths E3 to C4 (bar 41) and A-flat3 to F4 (bar 42), the alto's tritones A4 to E-flat4 (bar 48) and F4 to C-flat5 (bars 28 and 72); the bass's sixteenth on "be é-" (bar 13), the short half of a dotted pickup; the doubled C in bars 22, 23, 41, 50 and 70, the dominant of F minor there, not a leading note; the tenor above the alto in bars 48 and 50; the soprano and bass in octaves from D-flat to C on "gloi-re" (bar 70); and the tenor's D-flat over a C chord in bar 50, an appoggiatura.
licence.source: Écho des Maîtrises, collection nouvelle de chants religieux inédits des plus célèbres compositeurs modernes, publiée sous la direction de M. R. Bussine, première livraison, No. 10: Cantique de Jean Racine, chœur, "A Monsieur César Franck" (Paris: F. Schoen, undated, plate F. 309 S.; IMSLP dates a Schoen printing "[1876?]"), pp. 2 to 9, the earliest known printing; in D-flat, common time, Andante, written here in quarter-note beats as printed; the voices only. Read from the scan of the Bibliothèque nationale de France copy, Vmg. 17107 (I,10) (dépôt de la Société des Concerts du Conservatoire), digitized by Gallica.
